subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should managed Gateway install and refresh fail before rewriting the service when `gateway.auth.mode=none` would bind outside loopback?
rationale: The code matches the existing runtime security refusal, but moving the refusal into install/refresh changes when existing invalid managed installs fail and what operator action is required.

options.title: Accept the earlier install block
options.body: Keep the PR shape so invalid explicit no-auth non-loopback managed installs stop before service rewrite with an actionable remediation message.

options.title: Require fuller managed-service proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service run before accepting the compatibility change.

options.title: Pause for broader update proof
options.body: Leave the PR paused if maintainers want the original update mutation path proven before changing installer behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the earlier install block
recommendation.body: Keep the PR shape so invalid explicit no-auth non-loopback managed installs stop before service rewrite with an actionable remediation message.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior Gateway runtime and fail-closed bind/auth work makes this the strongest available routing owner for the compatibility/security-boundary choice.
